name: Dig Rat Stew
summary: Grub waits east of the Crossroads, hungry for a pot of dig rat stew. He sends travelers to Bael Modan in the southern Barrens to bring back dig rats for his recipe.

sections.title: Barrens Delicacies
sections.body: Across the dry Barrens, hunters bring down zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors. Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads, craves something different: dig rats. He says he is hungry all day and offers to share his recipe with any traveler willing to catch the burrowing rodents.

sections.title: The Dwarven Vermin
sections.body: Bael Modan lies deep in the southern Barrens, where dwarven prospectors dig into the red earth. Their work has disturbed nests of dig rats. The dwarves see the small rodents as an infestation, while Grub sees a feast close to the excavation.

sections.title: A Matter of Flavor
sections.body: Grub says dig rats taste best after rotting for several weeks. For a hungry traveler who wants food now, he accepts fresher meat. His recipe shows how forgiving roadside cooking can be on Kalimdor's frontier.

faq.answer: Grub is an orc camping along the trail east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. He is always hungry, has peculiar tastes, and will teach travelers to cook local vermin.

faq.q: Where do dig rats come from?
faq.answer: Dig rats infest Bael Modan, an Alliance excavation in the far southern Barrens, south of Camp Taurajo and north of Razorfen Kraul. The dwarves' mining disturbed the ground and brought swarms of the small creatures.

faq.q: Why does Grub want dig rats specifically?
faq.answer: Grub calls dig rats everyone's favorite feast and says hunting vermin is a rite of passage for seasoned travelers. They are the main ingredient in his hearty, pungent stew.

faq.q: Is Dig Rat Stew actually good to eat?
faq.answer: Grub calls it delicious, though his taste is extreme. He prefers the meat after it has rotted for a few weeks, making the stew an acquired taste even by rugged Horde standards.

faq.q: Why are there dwarves in Bael Modan?
faq.answer: The dwarves of Bael Modan are an Ironforge expedition. They built a keep and excavation in the southern Barrens, blasting and digging deep into the land; their presence has heightened tensions with the Horde and stirred up native vermin.

faq.q: Do you need special culinary training to make the stew?
faq.answer: Grub's method calls for basic hearthcraft and field dressing. Anyone with rudimentary cooking experience can learn to simmer the rodents into a sustaining meal.

angles.text: Preparing dig rat stew teaches frontier foraging: quarry vermin become a filling, foul-smelling campfire meal.
Taking dig rats from Bael Modan offers a way to mock the dwarven excavation while gathering rations in the southern Barrens.
Grub likes to let meat rot for weeks before boiling it, a taste few living cooks share with the Forsaken.
